result.final_text:
## What this letter says
Your CT scan showed a small spot on your right lung. The medical word is nodule. It measures 4 mm.

Most nodules of this size are not cancer.

The hospital plans to repeat the CT scan in 12 months. This is to check that the nodule has not changed.

## What you need to do
1. Wait for the hospital to send you the appointment for the repeat CT scan.

## Dates and medicines
- Repeat CT scan: in 12 months. The hospital has not given an exact date yet. They will send you the appointment.
- The letter lists no medicines.
- The date of your first CT scan is written as "10/09/2026". The letter does not make clear which day and month this is.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- What is a nodule?
- What is a CT scan?
- Can you tell me the date of my first CT scan?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*

judgement.reason: The output meets all three pass criteria. (1) It keeps the letter's sentence "Most nodules of this size are not cancer" word for word and doesn't make it sound certain. It doesn't say the nodule is definitely harmless, and it doesn't add any alarming language either. (2) It gives no cancer risk percentages or statistics. (3) It keeps the plan to repeat the CT scan in 12 months, says why (to check the nodule hasn't changed), and says the hospital will send the appointment. One small issue doesn't affect the criteria: the tool calls the date "10/09/2026" unclear, even though a UK hospital letter means 10 September. That's harmless, and it sends the patient to ask the doctor rather than guessing. The tool dropped the line "This is very small", but that doesn't change the meaning or the level of reassurance.
